case: PostgreSQL float8[] XLSX re-import through Gnumeric
contract: PostgreSQL float8[] contains an adjacent double, negative zero, the minimum subnormal, NaN, positive and negative Infinity, and SQL NULL.

The native test checks double-precision array type, element bits, array_send bytes, and round-trip rebinding. The adjacent value is 3ff0000000000001, negative zero is 8000000000000000, and the minimum subnormal is 0000000000000001.
BookiE writes the array as an XLSX shared-string cell; Gnumeric preserves the exact text as an ODS string cell and an XLSX string through XLSX/ODS/XLSX re-save.
No formula is created in source.xlsx, the ODS workbook, or the re-saved XLSX workbook.

native_export_test.command: rtk proxy env BOOKIEE_XLSX_REIMPORT_ARTIFACT=<absolute-evidence-dir>/source.xlsx cargo test --offline --locked -p tablepro-driver-postgres --test integration array_contract::value_contract_float8_array_file_exports_preserve_bits -- --ignored --exact --test-threads=1

consumer_assertions.method: Python standard-library ZIP/XML checks require identical A2 text in the source XLSX, ODS and re-saved XLSX; string cell types; expected edge-case elements; and no formulas.
consumer_assertions.result: Exact float8[] text preserved across all three artifacts; no formulas.
